paper.abstract: In this document, we introduce PyCSP$3$, a Python library that allows us to write models of combinatorial constrained problems in a declarative manner. Currently, with PyCSP$3$, you can write models of constraint satisfaction and optimization problems. More specifically, you can build CSP (Constraint Satisfaction Problem) and COP (Constraint Optimization Problem) models. Importantly, there is a complete separation between the modeling and solving phases: you write a model, you compile it (while providing some data) in order to generate an XCSP$3$ instance (file), and you solve that problem instance by means of a constraint solver. You can also directly pilot the solving procedure in PyCSP$3$, possibly conducting an incremental solving strategy. In this document, you will find all that you need to know about PyCSP$3$, with more than 50 illustrative models.
paper.title: PyCSP3: Modeling Combinatorial Constrained Problems in Python

paper.abstract: Motivated by widespread electrification targets, this paper studies an Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows and Nonlinear Charging (EVRPTWNL) that jointly optimizes routing-scheduling decisions and charging decisions given vehicle capacities, time windows and battery capacities. We develop a column generation scheme with a subpath-based label-setting algorithm that decomposes the pricing problem into two phases: (i) generating subpaths between charging stations, and (ii) combining subpaths into paths while optimizing charging decisions in between. We formalize a domination framework to establish the convergence and exactness of the algorithm, and prove that the methodology can solve a range of EVRP variants (e.g., with vehicle capacities, time windows, and nonlinear charging) and relaxation-tightening strategies (e.g., ng-relaxations and subset-row cuts). Computational results show improvements over path-based benchmarks in both computational time and solution quality, especially when time windows become wider, when vehicles can perform multiple tasks on a single charge and when vehicles still need to recharge several times across the planning horizon. Ultimately, the methodology can scale to otherwise intractable instances with up to 100 customers, thereby enhancing fleet management capabilities across electrified logistics areas.
paper.title: Subpath-Based Column Generation for Electric Vehicle Routing Problems

paper.abstract: Constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning offers the framework to design scalable and almost surely feasible solutions for teams of agents operating in dynamic environments to carry out conflicting tasks. We address the challenges of multi-agent coordination through an unconventional formulation in which the dual variables are not driven to convergence but are free to cycle, enabling agents to adapt their policies dynamically based on real-time constraint satisfaction levels. The coordination relies on a light single-bit communication protocol over a network with stochastic connectivity. Using this gossiped information, agents update local estimates of the dual variables. Furthermore, we modify the local dual dynamics by introducing a contraction factor, which lets us use finite communication buffers and keep the estimation error bounded. Under this model, we provide theoretical guarantees of almost sure feasibility and corroborate them with numerical experiments in which a team of robots successfully patrols multiple regions, communicating under a time-varying ad-hoc network.
paper.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems
paper.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Assignment over Stochastic Graphs via Constrained Reinforcement Learning

paper.abstract: The application of learning based methods to vehicle routing problems has emerged as a pivotal area of research in combinatorial optimization. These problems are characterized by vast solution spaces and intricate constraints, making traditional approaches such as exact mathematical models or heuristic methods prone to high computational overhead or reliant on the design of complex heuristic operators to achieve optimal or near optimal solutions. Meanwhile, although some recent learning-based methods can produce good performance for VRP with straightforward constraint scenarios, they often fail to effectively handle hard constraints that are common in practice. This study introduces a novel end-to-end framework that combines constraint-oriented hypergraphs with reinforcement learning to address vehicle routing problems. A central innovation of this work is the development of a constraint-oriented dynamic hyperedge reconstruction strategy within an encoder, which significantly enhances hypergraph representation learning. Additionally, the decoder leverages a double-pointer attention mechanism to iteratively generate solutions. The proposed model is trained by incorporating asynchronous parameter updates informed by hypergraph constraints and optimizing a dual loss function comprising constraint loss and policy gradient loss. The experiment results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach not only eliminates the need for sophisticated heuristic operators but also achieves substantial improvements in solution quality.
paper.title: Learning Constraints-Based Adaptive Hypergraph Neural Networks for Solving Vehicle Routing Problems

paper.abstract: Challenges in last-mile delivery have encouraged solutions like crowdsourced delivery, in which occasional drivers undertake delivery tasks along their pre-planned trips in exchange for compensation. A key challenge is that drivers' acceptance behavior towards offered tasks is uncertain and influenced by task properties and compensation. The current literature lacks formulations that address this challenge with a joint and exact approach. Hence, we formulate an integrated optimization problem that maximizes total expected cost savings by offering bundles of tasks to occasional drivers. We simultaneously determine the optimal set of bundles, their assignment to drivers, and personalized compensations for each bundle-driver pair while considering bundle- and compensation-dependent acceptance probabilities, captured via generic logistic functions. The vast number of potential bundles, combined with incorporating acceptance probabilities leads to a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) with exponentially many variables. We address these complexities by exploiting properties of the problem, leading to an exact linearization of the MINLP tackled via a tailored exact column generation algorithm. Our algorithm uses a variant of the elementary shortest path problem with resource constraints that features a non-linear and non-additive objective function as subproblem, for which we develop tailored dominance and pruning strategies. We introduce several heuristic and exact variants, and perform an extensive experiments evaluating the performance and the solution structures. The results demonstrate the efficiency of these algorithms for instances with up to 120 tasks and 60 drivers, and highlight the advantages of integrated decision-making over sequential approaches. The sensitivity analysis indicates that sensitivity to compensation is the most influential factor in shaping the bundle structure.
paper.title: Pricing, bundling, and driver behavior in crowdsourced delivery

analysis.analysis: 作者首先识别出分支定界框架中割选择与分支两个模块的紧密耦合关系，指出孤立学习策略的局限性。随后将这两个模块之间的协作关系形式化为Stackelberg博弈，区分领导者与跟随者的决策层级。基于该博弈结构，作者将联合优化视为非平稳学习问题，并采用两时间尺度更新规则来稳定并发训练。作者还通过数据通信的预训练阶段为各模块策略提供共享信息基础，再在第二阶段进行在线并发微调，以协调各模块策略。

paper.abstract: Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) has been a fundamental problem in combinatorial optimization. Conventional MILP solving mainly relies on carefully designed heuristics embedded in the branch-and-bound framework. Driven by the strong capabilities of neural networks, recent research is exploring the value of machine learning alongside conventional MILP solving. Although learning-based MILP methods have shown great promise, existing works typically learn policies for individual modules in MILP solvers in isolation, without considering their interdependence, which limits both solving efficiency and solution quality. To address this limitation, we propose Collab-Solver, a novel multi-agent-based policy learning framework for MILP that enables collaborative policy optimization for multiple modules. Specifically, we formulate the collaboration between cut selection and branching in MILP solving as a Stackelberg game. Under this formulation, we develop a two-phase learning paradigm to stabilize collaborative policy learning: the first phase performs data-communicated policy pretraining, and the second phase further orchestrates the policy learning for various modules. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and large-scale real-world MILP datasets demonstrate that the jointly learned policies significantly improve solving performance. Moreover, the policies learned by Collab-Solver have also demonstrated excellent generalization abilities across different instance sets.
paper.title: Collab-Solver: Collaborative Solving Policy Learning for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming

paper.abstract: Although the Maximum Clique Problem (MCP) has been extensively studied and features a rich ecosystem of exact solvers, empirical evidence shows that solver performance varies substantially across graph families. Consequently, selecting an appropriate algorithm for a given instance remains an open and practically important challenge that has received little systematic attention. We address this gap by developing an instance-aware selection framework that systematically combines global statistical descriptors with learned topological representations. We construct a comprehensive benchmark by evaluating four state-of-the-art exact solvers on a diverse collection of graph instances and deriving both global statistical and local structural features. An evaluation of conventional classifiers establishes Random Forest as a strong baseline and reveals that connectivity and topological features are key predictors of performance. Motivated by these observations, we introduce a dual-channel architecture that jointly leverages a Graph Attention Network for capturing local neighborhood patterns and a Multilayer Perceptron for modeling global statistical features. Extensive experiments show that the proposed dual-channel model consistently surpasses classical baselines and the single-best solver, achieving 90.43% test accuracy. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating local topological encoding with global statistical cues for combinatorial algorithm selection. Code and models are available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GAT-MLP-7E5F.
paper.title: Instance-Aware Algorithm Selection for Maximum Clique via a Dual-Channel Graph Neural Architecture

paper.abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance on Job Shop Scheduling (JSP) and Flexible JSP (FJSP) problems by learning scheduling policies through direct interaction with simulated environments. However, these methods often require extensive training interactions, limiting their sample efficiency and practical applicability. Motivated by this challenge, we introduce Conservative Discrete Quantile Actor-Critic (CDQAC), an offline RL algorithm that learns effective scheduling policies directly from static, suboptimal datasets. CDQAC couples a quantile-based critic with delayed policy updates to estimate the return distribution of machine-operation pairs. Extensive experiments on JSP and FJSP benchmarks demonstrate that CDQAC matches or outperforms the data-generating heuristics, outperforms recent offline and online RL baselines for JSP and FJSP, and is highly sample efficient, requiring only 1 to 5% of the original dataset to learn high-quality policies. Our analysis suggests that, for JSP and FJSP, offline RL performance depends more on state-action coverage than on the quality of individual trajectories. FJSP and JSP couple a dense reward aligned with the makespan objective with equal-length trajectories across heuristics, enabling effective learning from a broad range of behaviors. Consistent with this observation, datasets generated by a simple random heuristic with broader coverage let it outperform policies trained on datasets produced by stronger heuristics such as Genetic Algorithms. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/jesserem/CDQAC_scheduling.
paper.title: Generalizing Beyond Suboptimality: Offline Reinforcement Learning Learns Effective Scheduling through Random Solutions

在合成与受控数值实验中量化错误承诺、保留的改进与验证成本，并用后验分解区分零效应承诺的减少与严格有害承诺的减少。
一次两次尝试的ImageNet-100运行展示了一个被认证的检查点承诺，随后从被采纳状态训练出的候选被拒绝。
合成结果给出示例数字：在强效应0.25、路径强度0时，SGM每轨迹接受5.029个有益更新，逐测试确认接受5.358个，分别使用7,135与5,960个证据对；合成测试固定下注比例lambda=0.2，在增益0.10与0.05处期望对数财富增量非正。
在数值容差10^{-3}下，仅筛选采纳的每个错误承诺轨迹都包含严格有害更新；在所报告运行中SGM没有做出严格有害承诺，逐测试确认平均为每条轨迹0或0.0005个严格有害承诺；约98.7%–100%的合成FWER降低来自零效应错误轨迹而非有害承诺。
条件功效诊断：在合成IID {-1,+1}模型下，增益g=0.10时原检验在alpha=.05下功效为28.738%。
作者指出实验匹配轮次与单次尝试上限，而非实际总支出；这些结果不建立通用效用收益。
analysis.insight: 核心洞察在于：把哥德尔机“必须证明改进”的义务弱化为“在声明评估目标上以指定置信水平认证改进”，并用轨迹级误差预算把每次确认尝试的误判概率累积起来加以约束，从而在不要求全局未来效用比较的前提下，获得“从不接受非改进更新”的高概率保证。按材料，其有效性来自条件有效的确认检验与可预测、可求和的误差预算这一组合，而不是某个单独模块；CTHS则通过按确认事件而非轮次索引花费，把误差预算集中到有希望的修改上，同时保持族错误率有效性。
limitations: 框架只在声明的采样模型内有效；仅靠预算核算无法修复目标设定错误、确认数据被污染或评估器变更的问题。
形式结果只针对认证目标上的非改进，不约束灾难性尾部损失，不保证更低的总计算量，不保证取得进展，也不恢复经典哥德尔机的全局未来效用结果。
单调性额外要求共同效用与忠实的状态转移；分布变化需要新的有效采样论证，把时间分epoch并分配预算本身不能解决分布漂移。
受控工作负载展示的是效用已知的证书驱动配置变更；P2加入真实的训练状态转移与后续决策，但仅限一个初始化、两次尝试和受限的提议器，其证书针对固定有限池，留出集审计不估计总体风险。
评估学习系统中的误差校准与保留改进需要更长、独立重复的轨迹；历史学习轨迹仍是探索性的。
合成测试固定lambda=0.2，弱效应接受反映该证书的功效性质以及风险分配，低功效不能仅归因于全局预算。
method: SGM用统计置信检验（e-values、Hoeffding界）替代逐次更新的形式化证明，只有当候选在选定置信水平上被认证优于现任时才允许采纳。
框架将自适应提议生成与确认分离：提议器（proposer）给出候选，评估装置比较候选与现任，门控依据统计证书与分配的误差预算授权采纳。
分配全局误差预算以约束多轮累积风险；在对数上界下，接受非改进更新的概率不超过用户指定水平。
提出Confirm-Triggered Harmonic Spending（CTHS），按确认事件而不是按轮次索引花费，把误差预算集中于有希望的修改，同时保持族错误率有效性；CTHS是可选的分配实例而非框架前提。
对固定效用且状态转移忠实的情形，得到高概率非递减的现任效用序列，但不保证一定找到改进。
在协议中区分两类被采纳对象：检查点（checkpoint）与训练过程（training procedure）；替换未来随机执行的训练过程是另一种不同的决策，需要关于过程期望效用的证据。
analysis.motivation: 递归自修改在AutoML、神经架构搜索和自适应优化中日益核心，但现有框架无法保证这类修改被安全地做出。哥德尔机通过要求改写代码前给出改进的形式化证明来提供原则性保障，然而在随机、高维的学习系统中这类证明无法获得。因此作者希望用统计置信检验替代逐次更新的形式化证明，使基于证据的自我改进在经验设定中可执行，同时显式控制跨轮次的累积误采纳风险。
analysis.primary_topic: 学习系统递归自修改的风险受控统计认证机制
analysis.relation_to_research: 该文并不直接研究柔性作业车间、流水车间、分布式制造或生产运输协同等生产调度问题，也未给出调度实例、机器约束或能效目标，因此与当前生产调度主线属于弱到中等相关。论文事实层面，它提供的是学习系统递归自修改的统计采纳门控与轨迹级风险预算，可用于AutoML、神经架构搜索和黑盒优化等自适应优化环节。迁移设想（推测）：把SGM的门控与CTHS误差预算迁移到生产调度中的参数自适应、算法配置选择或进化算法算子选择，需要满足条件是——调度目标可定义为有界标量效用、能够从同一状态采集新鲜且条件有效的确认样本、状态转移在确认窗口内忠实、并且接受决策的误判代价可以用概率上界约束；否则预算核算本身无法修复目标错设或分布漂移，这一点作者明确说明。
analysis.setting: 论文研究一个自改进学习循环中的采纳决策问题：提议器（proposer）生成一个对当前代码或配置的修改候选（例如降低学习率、改变训练过程），评估装置（evaluation harness）在指定评估目标上比较候选与现任（incumbent），只有获得统计改进证书且满足轨迹级风险分配时，门控（gate）才授权采纳该修改；目标是把“接受非改进修改”的概率控制在用户指定水平，关键约束是随机、高维环境下无法获得形式化证明，且需要区分被采纳的对象是检查点（checkpoint）还是训练过程（training procedure），信息假设是确认测试条件有效且误差预算可预测、可求和，环境为跨轮次的序贯（动态）决策环境，材料未说明具体生产或调度场景。
analysis.title_zh: 统计哥德尔机：面向风险受控递归自修改的统计安全层
analysis.uncertainty: 输入材料为arXiv摘要与部分全文节选，正文片段存在截断和排版噪声（如公式与段落中断），无法核验全部实验表格、完整证明与消融细节；第一单位来自片段中的作者隶属信息，通讯作者未在材料中标注；相关性与可迁移性判断基于该文对自适应采纳决策的机制描述，而非其在生产调度上的直接证据。
analysis.why_recommended: 对关注AI4OR的研究者而言，该文的价值不在于给出新的调度算法，而在于提供一种把“何时采纳一次自修改/配置变更”形式化为统计认证问题的机制：轨迹级误差预算、按确认事件花费的CTHS以及检查点与训练过程两类采纳对象的区分，可为学习辅助搜索、在线算法配置和自适应算子选择中的采纳门控设计提供参考；同时作者对功效、误采纳与验证成本之间权衡以及分布漂移下论断边界的讨论，有助于在调度场景中避免把统计保证误当作性能保证。

paper.abstract: Recursive self-modification is increasingly central in AutoML, neural architecture search, and adaptive optimization, yet no existing framework ensures that such changes are made safely. Godel machines offer a principled safeguard by requiring formal proofs of improvement before rewriting code; however, such proofs are unattainable in stochastic, high-dimensional settings. We introduce the Statistical Godel Machine (SGM), the first statistical safety layer for recursive edits. SGM replaces proof-based requirements with statistical confidence tests (e-values, Hoeffding bounds), admitting a modification only when superiority is certified at a chosen confidence level, while allocating a global error budget to bound cumulative risk across rounds.We also propose Confirm-Triggered Harmonic Spending (CTHS), which indexes spending by confirmation events rather than rounds, concentrating the error budget on promising edits while preserving familywise validity.Experiments across supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and black-box optimization validate this role: SGM certifies genuine gains on CIFAR-100, rejects spurious improvement on ImageNet-100, and demonstrates robustness on RL and optimization benchmarks.Together, these results position SGM as foundational infrastructure for continual, risk-aware self-modification in learning systems.Code is available at: https://github.com/gravitywavelet/sgm-anon.
paper.title: SGM: A Statistical Godel Machine for Risk-Controlled Recursive Self-Modification

paper.abstract: Distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) has been studied for five decades, yet published algorithms are rarely compared under identical assumptions: authors report results on different test systems, with different power-flow models, and almost never release code. This paper re-implements eight representative DNR algorithms in a single open-source Python framework and benchmarks them on five networks under identical conditions. The algorithms span three of the four established paradigms: heuristics (loop cutting, branch exchange, greedy minimum spanning tree, exhaustive search), metaheuristics (a genetic algorithm and a selective binary particle swarm optimizer) and mathematical programming (a mixed-integer quadratic program built on a convex, simplified DistFlow power-flow model). We report power losses, voltage profile, and, as a hardware-independent cost metric, the number of power-flow evaluations required for convergence. On the 196-bus Simbench urban network, we show that a dynamic DNR policy can save more than 26% of the system losses, weighed against circuit-breaker maintenance cost. All implementations, test cases, and result scripts are released to allow direct extension and replication
paper.title: Distribution Network Reconfiguration: A Reproducible Benchmark of Heuristic, Metaheuristic and Mathematical Methods

analysis.analysis: 作者将问题建模为模型基强化学习，在每个分区内估计漂移、波动和奖励，通过统计置信区间判断估计偏差，偏差过大时细分分区。这类似于自适应网格细化，利用了扩散过程的局部平稳性。作者定义新的“变焦维度”来度量无界扩散过程中对学习真正重要的维度，并基于此建立遗憾界。该方法消解了连续域带来的维度灾难，同时将有界情形的现有界作为特例恢复。

paper.abstract: We study reinforcement learning for controlled diffusion processes with unbounded continuous state spaces, bounded continuous actions, and polynomially growing rewards: settings that arise naturally in finance, economics, and operations research. To overcome the challenges of continuous and high-dimensional domains, we introduce a model-based algorithm that adaptively partitions the joint state-action space. The algorithm maintains estimators of drift, volatility, and rewards within each partition, refining the discretization whenever estimation bias exceeds statistical confidence. This adaptive scheme balances exploration and approximation, enabling efficient learning in unbounded domains. Our analysis establishes regret bounds that depend on the problem horizon, state dimension, reward growth order, and a newly defined notion of zooming dimension tailored to unbounded diffusion processes. The bounds recover existing results for bounded settings as a special case, while extending theoretical guarantees to a broader class of diffusion-type problems. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our approach through numerical experiments, including applications to high-dimensional problems such as multi-asset mean-variance portfolio selection.
paper.title: Adaptive Partitioning and Learning for Stochastic Control of Diffusion Processes

paper.abstract: Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO) has mostly focused on learning policies, typically neural networks, that operate on a single candidate solution at a time, either by constructing one from scratch or iteratively improving it. In contrast, decades of work in metaheuristics have shown that maintaining and evolving populations of solutions improves robustness and exploration, and often leads to stronger performance. To close this gap, we study how to make NCO explicitly population-based by learning policies that act on sets of candidate solutions. We first propose a simple taxonomy of population awareness levels and use it to highlight two key design challenges: (i) how to represent a whole population inside a neural network, and (ii) how to learn population dynamics that balance intensification (generating good solutions) and diversification (maintaining variety). We make these ideas concrete with two complementary tools: one that improves existing solutions using information shared across the whole population, and the other generates new candidate solutions that explicitly balance being high-quality with diversity. Experimental results on Maximum Cut and Maximum Independent Set indicate that incorporating population structure is advantageous for learned optimization methods and opens new connections between NCO and classical population-based search.

paper.title: Enabling Population-Based Architectures for Neural Combinatorial Optimization

paper.abstract: Optimization benchmarks play a fundamental role in assessing algorithm performance; however, existing artificial benchmarks often fail to capture the diversity and irregularity of real-world problem structures, while benchmarks derived from real-world problems are costly and difficult to construct. To address these challenges, we propose an evolutionary automatic benchmark generation framework that leverages a large language model (LLM) as a generative operator, termed the LLM-driven evolutionary benchmark generator (LLM-EBG). In this framework, the LLM serves as an evolutionary operator that generates and evolves benchmark problems within a flexible, expressive representation space. As a case study, we generate unconstrained single-objective continuous minimization problems represented as mathematical expressions designed to induce significant performance differences between a genetic algorithm (GA) and differential evolution (DE). Experimental results show that LLM-EBG successfully produces benchmark problems in which the designated target algorithm consistently outperforms the comparative algorithm in more than 80\% of trials. Furthermore, exploratory landscape analysis reveals that benchmarks favoring GA are highly sensitive to variable scaling, demonstrating that the proposed framework can generate problems with distinct geometric characteristics that reflect the intrinsic search behaviors of different optimization algorithms.
paper.title: An Evolutionary Framework for Automatic Optimization Benchmark Generation via Large Language Models

paper.abstract: This paper proposes a novel Variational Graph-to-Scheduler (VG2S) framework for solving the Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP), a critical task in manufacturing that directly impacts operational efficiency and resource utilization. Conventional Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches often face challenges such as non-stationarity during training and limited generalization to unseen problem instances because they optimize representation learning and policy execution simultaneously. To address these issues, we introduce variational inference to the JSSP domain for the first time and derive a probabilistic objective based on the Evidence of Lower Bound (ELBO) with maximum entropy reinforcement learning. By mathematically decoupling representation learning from policy optimization, the VG2S framework enables the agent to learn robust structural representations of scheduling instances through a variational graph encoder. This approach significantly enhances training stability and robustness against hyperparameter variations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior zero-shot generalization compared with state-of-the-art DRL baselines and traditional dispatching rules, particularly on large-scale and challenging benchmark instances such as DMU and SWV.

paper.abstract: Constraint handling is central to constrained black-box optimization (BBO), where objective improvement and feasibility restoration often provide conflicting search signals. Existing $\epsilon$-relaxation methods are simple and effective, but their relaxation schedules are usually fixed or manually designed for a limited range of problems. To address this limitation, this letter proposes MeCO, a meta-learning-assisted optimizer that learns an adaptive $\epsilon$-relaxation policy for constrained BBO. MeCO couples a SHADE optimizer with a Double Deep Q-Network controller. At each optimization step, the controller observes compact population and constraint features and selects a scalar action, which is decoded into a relaxation vector for the candidate comparison rule. The policy is trained across constrained BBO instances and then deployed on held-out problems without problem-specific tuning. Experiments on the CEC2017 constrained benchmark, 16 UAV path-planning tasks and eight real-world engineering problems provide evidence that MeCO transfers across held-out benchmark functions, higher dimensions, and an application-domain setting. Ablation and behavior analyses further clarify the roles of constraint-related state features, action scaling, reward shaping, and meta-training.
paper.title: Meta-Learning-Assisted Constraint Relaxation for Constrained Black-Box Optimization

evidence.quote: We study this tradeoff through Uniform Facility Location (UniFL), a problem with applications in clustering, summarization, logistics, and supply chains. We propose a fully differentiable MPNN that incorporates approximation-algorithmic principles without solver supervision or discrete relaxations.

While this is essential for preserving worst-case guarantees, it may also restrict flexibility, i.e., the architecture is tailored to UniFL and may require non-trivial redesign to extend to richer variants such as non-uniform opening costs, capacitated facility location, or settings with additional side constraints.

与 SimpleUniformFL 非学习近似算法比较，回答 Q1 是否改进近似比。
在 2000 到 10000 个顶点的更大测试集上评估尺寸泛化（Q2）。
在城市地图数据集上评估。
与 KMeans++ 和 KMedoids++ 等可扩展聚类方法比较（Q3）。
聚类实验中报告了惯性（Inertia）和运行时间：例如 MPNN 初始化的 k-Means 在某个设定下惯性 132.438±1.077、时间 0.007±0.001，k-Medoids++ 惯性 170.904±1.258、时间 0.028±0.000，MPNN 初始化的 k-Medoids 惯性 161.600±1.148、时间 0.095±0.002（具体对照需结合原始表格）。
analysis.insight: 将经典分布式近似算法中的局部决策规则（基于半径刻画与概率性设施开启）嵌入可微分 MPNN，使网络在保持近似算法最坏情况保证的同时，能够通过端到端无监督训练对输入分布中的结构进行数据驱动的修正，从而在经验性能上超过非学习的近似算法并逼近整数线性规划。
limitations: 方法聚焦于 UniFL，继承了底层分布式近似算法的结构假设，这虽然对保持最坏情况保证至关重要，但可能限制灵活性。
架构针对 UniFL 定制，扩展到非均匀开启成本、容量设施选址或带额外约束的变体可能需要非平凡的重设计。
需要更紧的理论分析将学习到的消息传递与实例相关的近似行为联系起来，并理解梯度下降变体在何种条件下能成功最小化期望损失。
method: 提出全可微、无监督的消息传递图神经网络架构，镜像经典分布式近似算法的关键结构组件：用学习到的消息估计每个节点的信息性半径，并基于半径计算概率性设施开启概率。
消息传递网络在图上进行局部邻域信息聚合，输出每个节点的开启概率，无需求解器监督、无需离散松弛或梯度估计器。

paper.abstract: Neural networks, particularly message-passing neural networks (MPNNs), are increasingly used as heuristics for hard combinatorial optimization problems. Yet many learning-based methods rely on supervision, reinforcement learning, or gradient estimators, causing high computational cost, unstable training, or limited guarantees. Classical approximation algorithms provide worst-case guarantees but are non-differentiable and cannot adapt to structure in natural input distributions. We study this tradeoff through Uniform Facility Location (UniFL), a problem with applications in clustering, summarization, logistics, and supply chains. We propose a fully differentiable MPNN that incorporates approximation-algorithmic principles without solver supervision or discrete relaxations. The model has provable approximation guarantees and empirically improves on standard approximation algorithms, narrowing the gap to integer linear programming.
paper.title: Learning to Approximate Uniform Facility Location via Graph Neural Networks

paper.abstract: Although foundation models have achieved remarkable success in general domains, applying them to electroencephalography (EEG) analysis is constrained by substantial data requirements and large parameter counts, which incur prohibitive computational costs and impede deployment in resource-constrained clinical environments. General-purpose automated machine learning frameworks are likewise ill-suited to this domain, since exploration within an unbounded programmatic space fails to incorporate essential neurophysiological priors and frequently yields neuroscientifically implausible solutions. We therefore propose NeuroWeaver, a unified autonomous evolutionary agent that generalizes across diverse EEG datasets and tasks by reformulating pipeline engineering as a discrete constrained optimization problem solved through large language model (LLM)-driven generation of executable code. A Domain-Informed Subspace Initialization confines the search to a neuroscientifically plausible manifold, while a Multi-Objective Evolutionary Optimization dynamically balances performance, novelty, and efficiency via self-reflective refinement. Across five heterogeneous benchmarks, NeuroWeaver synthesizes lightweight pipelines that outperform state-of-the-art task-specific methods on nearly all metrics and attain accuracy comparable to large-scale foundation models, even surpassing them on the HMC and Workload benchmarks with only $0.18$M and $0.011$M parameters, respectively.
paper.title: NeuroWeaver: An Autonomous Evolutionary Agent for Exploring the Programmatic Space of EEG Analysis Pipelines

paper.abstract: Automating heuristic design in complex, experiment-driven domains requires more than iterative mutation of solution algorithms. Current LLM-based evolutionary methods often rely on stochastic mutation loops that lack long-term strategic planning and a formal mechanism to learn from historical failures, leading to inefficient exploration and redundant trials. To address this, we present OR-Agent, a multi-agent research framework designed for automated heuristic design in optimization problems with rich experimental environments. OR-Agent organizes heuristic search as tree-based workflow that explicitly models branching hypothesis generation and systematic backtracking. Furthermore, to address the lack of adaptive learning in current agents, we introduce a hierarchical, optimization-inspired reflection system in which short-term reflections act as verbal gradients, long-term reflections as verbal momentum, and memory compression as semantic weight decay - collectively forming a principled mechanism for governing research dynamics. Extensive experiments on classical combinatorial optimization problems (e.g., TSP, CVRP, bin packing) and simulation-based cooperative driving scenarios demonstrate that OR-Agent outperforms strong evolutionary search baselines. All code and experimental data are publicly available at https://github.com/qiliuchn/OR-Agent.
paper.title: OR-Agent: Bridging Evolutionary Search and Structured Research for Automated Heuristic Design

analysis.uncertainty: 论文仅涉及随机 k-SAT 和 k-XORSAT，未涉及生产调度，且摘要未提供具体方法细节和实验数字，因此对其方法可迁移性的判断不确定。
analysis.why_recommended: 尽管论文不直接解决调度问题，但它提供了对离散生成模型在约束满足问题上的理论洞见，特别是变量排序和扩散模型的选择影响解质量。对于研究神经求解器或学习辅助搜索的研究者，了解这些现象有助于设计更有效的解码或生成策略。此外，随机约束满足问题的分析或可作为基准工具，用于评估生成模型在约束可行性方面的表现。

paper.abstract: Generating data from discrete distributions is important for a number of application domains including text, tabular data, and genomic data. Several groups have recently used random $k$-satisfiability ($k$-SAT) as a synthetic benchmark for new generative techniques. In this paper, we show that fundamental insights from the theory of random constraint satisfaction problems have observable implications (sometime contradicting intuition) on the behavior of generative techniques on such benchmarks. More precisely, we study the problem of generating a uniformly random solution of a given (random) $k$-SAT or $k$-XORSAT formula. Among other findings, we observe that: $(i)$~Continuous diffusions outperform masked discrete diffusions; $(ii)$~Learned diffusions can match the theoretical `ideal' accuracy; $(iii)$~Smart ordering of the variables can significantly improve accuracy, although not following popular heuristics.
paper.title: Generating from Discrete Distributions Using Diffusions: Insights from Random Constraint Satisfaction Problems

analysis.analysis: 作者沿用分支定价框架，将问题分解为高层定价（生成候选tour）和低层代价计算。关键分析在于识别出「tour代价计算」是MT-VRP-O相对于已有VRP的额外瓶颈，并据此设计惰性求值机制：只有在剪枝或加列检查无法用下界判定时才触发精确最短路径搜索。低层代价计算被建模为凸集图上的最短路径问题（SPP-GCS），并引入同时考虑目标剩余轨迹距离与障碍的启发式来加速搜索。
challenges: 在同时存在移动目标和静态障碍时，单智能体tour代价的精确计算（最短路径搜索）显著比传统VRP昂贵
需要在分支定价中维护下界与真实代价之间的一致性，以保证剪枝正确且最终获得最优解
静态障碍破坏原有连续性松弛假设，需要设计障碍感知的连续性松弛策略
在图结构中搜索最短路径时，启发式需要同时考虑目标剩余轨迹距离和障碍规避，以加速精确代价的获取

evidence.quote: The key idea in Lazy BPRC is to use cheap-to-compute lower bounds on tour costs where costs are traditionally used, and lazily update lower bounds to true costs.

evidence.quote: When computing a tour’s true cost is needed, we do so by searching for a shortest path on a graph of convex sets, and we introduce a new heuristic to accelerate the search.

experiments: 实验在Intel i9-9820X 3.3GHz CPU（10核，关闭超线程，128GB RAM）上进行；由于已有工作没有MT-VRP-O的基线，作者将Lazy BPRC与两个消融算法对比
第一个消融为Non-Lazy BPRC：在labeling算法生成tour并通过检查后，立即计算精确代价c*(Γ)并替换原有的UB与LB，再重新执行检查
第二个消融为Ignore-Obstacles-Heuristic：将GCS搜索中作者的启发式替换为文献[10]中不考虑障碍的启发式，即将max{dist(τa,rem), h_n(t)}替换为dist(τa,rem)
实例生成基于修改文献[15]的方法以支持多智能体；每个目标有两个时间窗，需求为1，每个时间窗内速度在0.5至1 m/s之间均匀随机生成；每个实例三个智能体，最大速度v_max=4 m/s
障碍地图为方形网格，但智能体与目标在网格中的连续空间移动；GCS中的区域由未占用网格单元组合而成的矩形构成
实验1改变随机网格中的目标数量，并测试来自文献[20]的迷宫地图；在迷宫图中Non-Lazy BPRC的中位运行时间达到时间上限，因此作者用9个目标对其n_seg,tar进行了调参
作者报告Lazy BPRC相比Non-Lazy消融的运行速度最多快43倍，相比使用忽略障碍的已有启发式的消融最多快23倍
作者观察到在某些实例中Lazy BPRC有时会不如Ignore-Obstacles-Heuristic消融，说明惰性机制并非在所有情况下都占优

analysis.insight: 核心洞察在于：分支定价的剪枝过程并不总是需要tour的精确代价，许多候选tour最终会被丢弃，因此在传统需要精确代价的位置上先使用易于计算且可安全用于剪枝的下界，仅在必要时才「惰性」地将其更新为真实代价，可在不牺牲最优性的前提下大幅减少高成本的精确轨迹搜索调用次数；同时障碍感知的连续性松弛策略使下界在存在障碍时仍然有效。
limitations: 作者在结论中明确指出未来工作方向之一是追求有界次优解以扩展到更多目标，暗示当前精确算法在目标数量上的可扩展性受限
实验对比仅使用两个消融算法，因为作者声明已有文献中不存在针对MT-VRP-O的基线
method: 在分支定价中，对每个候选tour先使用易计算的下界LB(Γ)，替代传统立即精确计算c*(Γ)，并进行剪枝与加列检查
当且仅当LB无法判定tour是否应被保留或丢弃时，才计算tour的真实代价c*(Γ)，并更新UB与LB后重新执行检查
精确tour代价通过求解GCS（graph of convex sets）上的最短路径问题（SPP-GCS）获得，其中环境中的无障碍单元格组合为矩形区域
引入一种新的障碍感知启发式，在GCS最短路径搜索中同时利用目标剩余轨迹距离和障碍信息，替代已有工作中忽略障碍的启发式
将已有的无目标障碍VRP中的连续性松弛扩展为障碍感知的连续性松弛，以适配MT-VRP-O中的静态障碍
在定价中的后继生成和GCS搜索中并行化计算，并对segment-to-segment及segment-start-to-segment-start的轨迹代价并行计算
analysis.motivation: 已有分支定价框架（BPRC）可用于无移动目标的传统VRP，但在MT-VRP-O中，由于同时存在移动目标和静态障碍，逐个精确计算tour代价（单智能体访问给定目标序列的路径代价）代价高昂，导致传统分支定价在每个候选序列上都精确算代价的做法效率低下，需要一种机制来避免不必要的精确代价计算。
analysis.primary_topic: 带时间窗与障碍的移动目标车辆路径问题的精确分支定价求解
analysis.relation_to_research: 该论文研究的是带时间窗和障碍的移动目标多智能体路径规划，属于车辆路径问题的精确求解分支，与生产调度和AI4OR中的分支定价技术有方法层面的关联：惰性代价求值、下界驱动的剪枝策略以及列生成思想可迁移到调度与路径协同优化中。但该文不涉及柔性作业车间、流水车间、能效或多目标进化算法；其低层最短路径搜索和凸集图方法也与图神经网络或强化学习求解调度问题无直接联系。若要在生产调度中应用类似思路，推测需要将「tour代价」替换为调度子问题的代价评估，并设计适配调度约束的下界与惰性更新机制，这仅是迁移设想而非作者结论。
analysis.setting: 研究多个智能体协作拦截一组移动目标的问题（MT-VRP-O），决策对象是每个智能体访问目标-时间窗配对的序列（tour）以及对应的拦截轨迹，目标是最小化总路径代价，关键约束包括：每个目标有一个或多个可访问时间窗、智能体必须避开静态障碍、满足速度上限与容量限制；假设目标轨迹在每个时间窗内为匀速分段线性且不穿过障碍，智能体与目标在同一连续空间内运动，环境为各目标与智能体同时运动的动态场景。
analysis.title_zh: 带障碍移动目标车辆路径问题的精确求解：惰性分支定价算法
analysis.uncertainty: 提供的全文节选缺少完整的数值结果表格、运行时间分布的详细数据以及更完整的算法伪代码，导致对实验规模（如目标数量的具体范围、时间上限具体数值）和调参细节的把握不完整；此外，没有提供与生产调度直接相关的实验，因此其迁移价值判断存在较大不确定性。
analysis.why_recommended: 对于关注精确求解框架与学习/搜索结合的研究者，该文的惰性求值与下界驱动剪枝机制提供了一种减少昂贵子问题求解调用的通用思路，可能启发在分支定价或分支切割框架中类似地设计「用廉价下界替代精确子问题求解」的策略，适用于生产调度中需要频繁评估子问题代价的场景。此外，其将GCS上的最短路径搜索与障碍感知启发式结合的方式，对多智能体协同路径规划有参考价值。

paper.abstract: The Moving Target Vehicle Routing Problem with Obstacles (MT-VRP-O) seeks trajectories for several agents that collectively intercept a set of moving targets. Each target has one or more time windows where it can be visited, and the agents must avoid static obstacles and satisfy speed and capacity constraints. Previously studied VRPs are often addressed using a framework called branch-and-price. This framework requires computing the cost for a single agent to visit a given sequence of target-time window pairings, for several candidate sequences. These sequences are called tours. Computing tour costs is more expensive in the MT-VRP-O than in previously studied VRPs due to the presence of both moving targets and static obstacles. Thus, we introduce a new exact algorithm, Lazy Branch-and-Price with Relaxed Continuity (Lazy BPRC), for the MT-VRP-O. The key idea in Lazy BPRC is to use cheap-to-compute lower bounds on tour costs where costs are traditionally used, and lazily update lower bounds to true costs. When computing a tour's true cost is needed, we do so by searching for a shortest path on a graph of convex sets, and we introduce a new heuristic to accelerate the search. We demonstrate that Lazy BPRC runs up to an order of magnitude faster than two ablations.
paper.title: Optimal Solutions for the Moving Target Vehicle Routing Problem with Obstacles via Lazy Branch-and-Price

analysis.analysis: 作者通过三个研究问题组织分析：RQ1 考察同一引擎能否在不做框架级修改的情况下支持不同算法设计域；RQ2 考察过程性快照能否跨数据集和兼容优化域迁移；RQ3 考察迁移在什么条件下产生收益。分析手段包括分层消融（L0 本体、L1 算子质量、L2 排序）来定位迁移粒度，用随机排序替换学习到的边权作为对照，用图上的联合分布、逐边分布、平稳分布与谱间隙来分析所学策略是否稳定未坍塌，并通过扰动边权检查执行器输出是否平滑有界。作者还用代理保真度表检验 NAS 表格基准的秩保真性，并明确把执行器定位为可复用的过程性先验而非专用求解器。
challenges: 如何将过程性知识表示为既能生成、又能执行、还可迁移的形式，同时不依赖部署时的语言模型调用
如何在跨数据集和跨领域两种不同粒度上界定并验证到底迁移了什么
如何设计 RoleSchema 使其同时具备语义约束力与跨域复用能力，而不至于只是限制搜索空间
如何在目标侧搜索成本低廉或已有强局部搜索时避免迁移带来的无效开销
当前图无在线自适应，如何在不破坏已学结构的前提下支持在线更新与顺序多域迁移

evidence.claim: 论文提出 GEAKG，将算法设计中的过程性知识表示为可生成、可执行、可迁移的图。
evidence.quote: We introduce Generative Executable Algorithm Knowledge Graphs (GEAKG), a representation in which this knowledge is stored as a generative, executable, transferable graph: typed nodes hold validated operators, edges encode admissible compositions, and learned edge weights record effective sequences.

evidence.claim: 同一引擎通过只更换 RoleSchema 与 binding 即可跨域实例化。
evidence.quote: The same engine instantiates the structure across domains by changing only a role ontology (RoleSchema) and a binding.

evidence.claim: 迁移内容取决于粒度：NAS 族内权重可迁移，跨组合域只有本体约束的可执行结构迁移。
evidence.quote: Layer ablations localize transfer by granularity: within a neural-architecture-search family the learned snapshot transfers across 70 dataset pairs—its weights stay correlated across datasets and one frozen snapshot remains competitive with Regularized Evolution at zero deployment-token cost; across combinatorial domains only the ontology-constrained executable structure transfers, not the learned weights.

evidence.claim: 迁移收益取决于目标侧搜索成本，在大规模调度实例上有收益，在分配和线性排序上无改善。
evidence.quote: That structure pays off where target-side search is expensive—a Traveling Salesman snapshot beats an equally untuned from-scratch search on large scheduling instances even at one-fifth its budget—but does not improve on an effective local search where one is cheap, as in assignment and linear ordering.

evidence.claim: 可执行过程性知识可离线获取、压缩、检视并复用，且运行时不调用语言模型。
evidence.quote: Executable procedural knowledge can thus be acquired offline, compacted, inspected, and reused without runtime language-model calls.

evidence.claim: 论文明确将 GEAKG 定位为表示机制而非最先进优化器。
evidence.quote: We study GEAKG as a representation mechanism rather than a state-of-the-art optimizer, asking what transfers and when.

evidence.claim: 零样本迁移部署使用固定快照，无目标域边权再训练、无算子重生成、无运行时语言模型调用。
evidence.quote: A target-domain deployment uses a fixed snapshot consisting of L0, L1, and L2. There is no target-domain edge weight retraining, no operator resynthesis, and no language-model call at runtime.

evidence.claim: 图无在线自适应，部署时使用固定转移权重与规则；快照只读，顺序多域迁移不产生灾难性遗忘。
evidence.quote: The graph also has no online adaptation. During deployment, the Symbolic Executor applies fixed transition weights and rules.

experiments: NAS 与组合优化两个领域共享同一 GEAKG 构建管线、快照格式、ACO 学习循环与 Symbolic Executor，差异限于 RoleSchema 与评估 candidate 所用的 binding
NAS 族内迁移：学习到的快照跨 70 个数据集对迁移，权重在数据集间保持相关，一个冻结快照在零部署 token 成本下仍与 Regularized Evolution 具有竞争力
NAS 保真度检查：NAS-Bench-201/NATS-Bench 表格精度在每数据集 1500 个架构上，CIFAR-10 跨种子 ρ=0.985、12ep→200ep ρ=0.875、种子噪声 0.17pp、Top-10 重叠 0.40；CIFAR-100 对应为 0.982、0.829、0.33、0.40；ImageNet16-120 为 0.988、0.812、0.37、0.50
NAS 选择结果：CIFAR-10 源上 Symbolic Executor 达 94.34%，距真实训练全局最优 94.37% 仅差 0.03 个百分点；零样本迁移到 CIFAR-100 达 71.13±0.11%，而 Regularized Evolution 在匹配 50 次评估预算下为 70.43%；其运行间标准差 0.11pp 小于基准自身 CIFAR-100 种子噪声 0.33pp
作者强调单个最佳架构身份对种子敏感：只有 40–50% 的 top-10 架构跨种子复现，因此应声称秩保真的顶层选择，而非唯一最优精确恢复
与 Random Search 对比：GEAKG 在 70/70 的平均精度提升，62/70 在 p<0.05 显著；与 Regularized Evolution 对比在 NAS-Bench-Graph 上中位提升 +0.13 个百分点，仅 10/64 对显著
跨组合优化域：本体约束的可执行结构在 JSSP 与 QAP 上保持可执行，JSSP 结果显示迁移在更大实例上最强；一个 TSP 快照即使只给五分之一预算也能在大规模调度实例上击败同等未调优的从头搜索，但在分配和线性排序这类廉价强局部搜索上并无改善
优化迁移实验规模：JSSP 用八种子运行，QAP 用五种子并覆盖八个 QAPLIB 实例
消融：随机排序替换学习边权会移除全迁移对上的优势；L0 消融显示模式通过降低搜索间隙产生经验贡献；当前消融逐层隔离 L0、L1、L2，未做含交互项的全因子分解
边权结构分析：NAS Cora GEAKG 中 42 条边有 9 条（21%）饱和于 τmax=1.0，14 条（33%）趋近 τmin；全边权范围 0.04 到 1.0，均值 0.51；学习分布相对均匀最大熵降低 3–4%，在 MMAS 界内理论最大降低约 15–20%；平稳质量集中于 act_mixed，π=0.14，谱间隙 0.19，扰动边权输出平滑有界
快照只读性验证：JSSP→QAP→JSSP 部署链后用哈希校验，学习边权状态在部署前后逐字节一致，因此按构造不存在灾难性遗忘

analysis.motivation: 算法设计中的过程性知识通常嵌在源代码、实验日志或隐性设计实践中，每当更换领域就需要重建、调参或重新演化，导致知识难以获取、检视和复用。作者希望将这类知识从源代码中解耦出来，变成一种可生成、可执行、可迁移的图表示，从而支持离线获取、压缩、检视与零语言模型调用的在线部署。

analysis.relation_to_research: 与智能优化和生产调度高度相关：论文直接以 JSSP 和 TSP 等排列式组合优化为实例，用 ACO 在图上学习算子转移权重，并把在 TSP 上得到的快照迁移到大规模调度实例，这属于学习辅助搜索与跨问题知识迁移。其“执行图 + 角色本体 + 学习边权”的机制可为柔性作业车间、流水车间等调度问题提供一种把构造、扰动、局部搜索算子组织成可复用先验的建模方式。迁移设想需明确为推测：若要把 GEAKG 迁到柔性作业车间或生产运输协同问题，需要先定义覆盖机器分配、工序排序与运输决策的 RoleSchema，并提供能评估可行性、时间窗与多目标代价的 binding；跨域权重能否直接复用需重新验证，因为作者已表明跨组合域时只有本体约束的可执行结构迁移，权重未必迁移；而若目标问题已有廉价且强的局部搜索，按作者结论迁移结构可能无额外收益。
analysis.setting: 论文研究算法设计中的过程性知识（procedural knowledge）如何表示、获取与迁移的问题。决策对象是算法设计过程中的算子选择与算子组合顺序，目标是在更换目标领域时以极低边际成本复用已学得的过程性知识，而非追求超越专用最先进求解器。关键约束包括：节点必须承载经过验证的可执行算子，边只能表示模式允许的合法组合，RoleSchema 决定角色本体，部署阶段必须零语言模型调用、不做目标域边权再训练；信息假设是目标域需暴露兼容的 binding 接口（提供评估、有效性检查、复制等操作）；环境涵盖静态的离线生成与学习阶段，以及在线符号执行阶段，作者将图设计为无在线自适应，学习到的边权在部署中固定不变。

paper.abstract: Procedural knowledge in algorithm design is embedded in source code and rebuilt for each new domain. We introduce Generative Executable Algorithm Knowledge Graphs (GEAKG), a representation in which this knowledge is stored as a generative, executable, transferable graph: typed nodes hold validated operators, edges encode admissible compositions, and learned edge weights record effective sequences. The same engine instantiates the structure across domains by changing only a role ontology (RoleSchema) and a binding. We study GEAKG as a representation mechanism rather than a state-of-the-art optimizer, asking what transfers and when. Layer ablations localize transfer by granularity: within a neural-architecture-search family the learned snapshot transfers across 70 dataset pairs - its weights stay correlated across datasets and one frozen snapshot remains competitive with Regularized Evolution at zero deployment-token cost; across combinatorial domains only the ontology-constrained executable structure transfers, not the learned weights. That structure pays off where target-side search is expensive - a Traveling Salesman snapshot beats an equally untuned from-scratch search on large scheduling instances even at one-fifth its budget - but does not improve on an effective local search where one is cheap, as in assignment and linear ordering. Executable procedural knowledge can thus be acquired offline, compacted, inspected, and reused without runtime language-model calls.
paper.title: Transferable knowledge graphs with executable learned operators for algorithm design

paper.abstract: We propose a hybrid reinforcement learning (RL) and model predictive control (MPC) framework for mixed-integer optimal control, where discrete variables enter the cost and dynamics but not the constraints. Existing hierarchical approaches learn a policy only for the discrete action space, leaving continuous optimization to MPC. Unlike these methods, we train an RL agent on the full hybrid action space, such that the learned critic approximates the Q-function of the underlying Markov decision process. During deployment, the RL actor is rolled out over the prediction horizon to parametrize an integer-free nonlinear MPC through the discrete action sequence and provide a continuous warm-start. The learned critic can additionally serve as a terminal cost to capture long-term performance. We prove recursive feasibility, and validate the framework on a Formula 1 race strategy problem, where an ablation study identifies the contribution of each learned component. The hybrid method achieves near-optimal performance relative to an offline mixed-integer nonlinear program benchmark, outperforming a standalone RL agent. Moreover, the hybrid scheme enables adaptation to unseen disturbances through modular MPC extensions at zero retraining cost.

paper.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving increasingly beyond prediction to support decisions in complex, uncertain, and dynamic environments. This shift creates a natural intersection with operations research and management science (OR/MS), which has long provided methodological foundations for sequential decision making under uncertainty. At the same time, deep learning advances, including feedforward neural networks, recurrent architectures, transformers, large language models (LLMs), and deep reinforcement learning, have expanded data-driven modeling for large-scale decisions. This tutorial presents an OR/MS-centered perspective on deep learning for sequential decision making under uncertainty, bridging neural architectures and OR/MS approaches to decision making. Its premise: deep learning complements optimization rather than replacing it. Deep learning brings adaptability and scalable approximation, whereas OR/MS provides the mathematical rigor to represent constraints, recourse, uncertainty, and decision quality. The tutorial reviews key decision making foundations, connects them to the major neural architectures in modern AI, and organizes the field around three central themes: predict-then-optimize and decision-aware learning, learning-based decision generation under constraints for continuous and discrete problems with temporal coupling, and deep reinforcement learning for sequential and combinatorial decision making. Impact spans supply chains, service systems, healthcare and epidemic response, agriculture, energy, environmental sustainability, and autonomous operations. This tutorial frames these developments as part of a shift from predictive AI toward decision-capable AI, highlighting OR/MS's role in shaping the next generation of integrated learning--optimization systems.
paper.title: Deep Learning for Sequential Decision Making under Uncertainty: Foundations, Frameworks, and Frontiers

paper.abstract: Efficient job-shop scheduling with transportation resources is critical for high-performance manufacturing. With the rise of "decentralized factories", multi-agent reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach for the combined scheduling of production and transportation tasks. Prior work has largely focused on developing novel cooperative architectures while overlooking the question of when joint training is necessary. Joint training denotes the simultaneous training of job and automatic guided vehicle scheduling agents, whereas modular training involves independently training each agent followed by post-hoc integration. In this study, we systematically investigate the conditions under which joint training is essential for optimal performance in the job-shop scheduling problem with transportation resources. Through a rigorous sensitivity analysis of resource scarcity and temporal dominance, we quantify the coordination gap -- the performance difference between these two training modalities. In our evaluation, joint training outperforms the majority of dispatching rule combinations and modular training approaches. However, the coordination gap advantage diminishes in bottleneck environments, particularly under severe transport and processing constraints. These findings indicate that modular training represents a viable alternative in environments where a single scheduling task dominates. Overall, our work provides practical guidance for selecting between training modalities based on environmental conditions, enabling decision-makers to optimize reinforcement learning-based scheduling performance.
paper.comment: This paper has been accepted for presentation at the IEEE 22st International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE 2026)
paper.title: An Analysis of the Coordination Gap between Joint and Modular Learning for Job Shop Scheduling with Transportation Resources

analysis.analysis: 作者利用问题的多阶段结构，将时间索引 MILP 重构为事件驱动动态规划：模式切换决定变长事件边界，事件内部由模式特定 LP 刻画连续运行。通过证明事件驱动表述与传统时间索引 MILP 等价，并在有限离散事件路径上枚举、对边界耦合多面体缩放，构造出精确的有限维凸包 LP。进一步对连续边界状态做事件边界网格离散，得到有限网格 LP，并分析其可行集与阶段式离散化的包含关系及线性于网格分辨率的误差界。另以事件驱动分支定界，仅对离散事件决策分支、用基于 McCormick 的 LP 松弛定界，作为连续状态重构的独立计算验证。

paper.abstract: Pumped-storage hydropower scheduling couples discrete operating-mode transitions with continuous dispatch decisions through intertemporal reservoir and ramping constraints. Existing convexification methods do not simultaneously accommodate multiple operating modes, persistent continuous reservoir and ramping states, and interval costs that depend on both incoming and outgoing states of the operating modes. We develop an event-based dynamic programming formulation in which mode transitions define variable-length events and mode-specific linear programs optimize continuous within-event operation. We prove that this formulation is equivalent to the conventional time-indexed mixed-integer linear program. Enumerating the finite set of discrete event paths and scaling their boundary-coupled polyhedra then yields an exact finite-dimensional convex-hull LP without state discretization. For tractability, we develop a finite-grid formulation that discretizes reservoir and ramping states only at event boundaries while retaining continuous within-event trajectories. Its feasible set contains that of the corresponding stagewise discretization. Moreover, the resulting LP provides an exact convex-hull representation of the grid-restricted model and admits an error bound linear in the grid resolutions. An event-based branch-and-bound method provides an independent computational verification of the continuous-state reformulation. Standalone experiments verify the theoretical results, while tests on a modified IEEE 24-bus Reliability Test System show that the finite-grid LP substantially reduces computation time with a negligible increase in system cost.
paper.title: Pumped-Storage Hydropower Scheduling: An Event-based Convex-hull Approach

paper.abstract: We present a novel framework for embedding hard constraint satisfaction into neural network (NN) architectures, specifically feedforward neural networks and transformers, with input-dependent affine constraints of arbitrary cardinality. Traditional constraint enforcement approaches either rely on penalty-based soft constraints, which offer no guarantee of satisfaction, or on post-processing methods that enforce constraints after the NN is trained, which may lead to suboptimality. We introduce a trainable constraint-affine (CAffine) layer into NNs, yielding CAffNet, which goes beyond enforcing affine constraints via fixed orthogonal or parallel projections and enables joint optimization with network parameters. Moreover, we impose no restrictions on the constraint space dimensions and establish that our construction preserves the universal approximation properties of NNs, while providing provable guarantees on constraint adherence for all inputs. Experimental validation demonstrates robust performance across diverse domains requiring guaranteed constraint satisfaction. The code is available at https://github.com/ice-t-lab/CAffNet.git.
paper.title: CAffNet: Hard Constraint-Affine Neural Networks

paper.abstract: Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically formulate and solve optimization problems from natural language has emerged as an efficient paradigm for automated optimization. However, existing methods still exhibit limited generalization: they are sensitive to superficial narrative variations, reuse experience mainly at the case level, and struggle to adapt to shifted or emerging problem types. We propose OptSkills, an archetype-centric skill learning and reasoning agent system for optimization modeling and solving. To improve robust generalization, our system clusters problems by their underlying archetypes rather than surface narratives. To improve in-distribution generalization, it explores diverse modeling paradigms and solver configurations within each cluster, then distills successful trajectories into reusable workflow-level skills. To improve out-of-distribution generalization, it refines existing skills or expands the skill library using newly obtained trajectories. Our system achieves a state-of-the-art micro-averaged accuracy of 68.27% on datasets encompassing diverse problem types and scenarios. In addition, on MIPLIB-NL, a highly challenging large-scale and high-dimensional benchmark, it achieves 26.91% accuracy, outperforming DeepSeek-V3.2-Thinking by 4.53%. After skill learning on Nano-CO, it reaches 72.79% on the OOD NLCO benchmark. Code and skills are available at https://github.com/fujiwaranoM0kou/OptSkills.
paper.comment: Accepted by Findings of EMNLP 2026, project: https://github.com/fujiwaranoM0kou/OptSkills
paper.title: OptSkills: Learning Generalizable Optimization Skills from Problem Archetypes via Cluster-Based Distillation

A slight change in relative poses can open large empty regions and shift occupancy by several points.
figures.label: Figure 1

figures.caption: PoT encoding pipeline. Each input polygon’s contour is uniformly resampled and grouped into local patches, which are tokenized and projected by an MLP. Tokens are then augmented with cyclic positional embeddings (encoding position within each polygon’s closed contour) and polygon ID embeddings (identifying which polygon a token belongs to), before self-attention is applied across the full multi-polygon sequence to yield one geometry-aware embedding per polygon.
figures.label: Figure 2

paper.abstract: Traditional heuristic solvers for the 2D irregular nesting problem share a fundamental limitation: they are blind to polygon geometry, relying on guided brute-force to navigate the continuous placement space with minimal geometrical guidance. In this paper, we argue that Reinforcement Learning is uniquely positioned to overcome this bottleneck. By pairing an optimization policy with a geometry-aware neural encoder, an agent can automatically discover rich geometric priors directly from data, utilizing these learned intuitions to strategically guide exploration. To realize this, we introduce the Polygons Transformer (PoT), a novel architecture that encodes 2D continuous vector geometries while allowing cross-polygon attention. We couple this novel architecture with a Combinatorial Optimization Reinforcement Learning (CORL) training framework to find optimal solutions. To support this paradigm, we release an open-source training dataset derived from complex geographic contours alongside a dedicated evaluation benchmark. Empirically, our agent slightly exceeds Sparrow, the state-of-the-art heuristic, on small (4-polygon) instances, while a clear scaling gap remains on larger (8-polygon) instances.
paper.comment: 20 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables. Under review at the Transaction on Machine Learning Research (TMLR)
paper.title: Geometry-Aware Reinforcement Learning for 2D Irregular Nesting

paper.abstract: The PDHG algorithm provides a new capability for solving difficult linear programming (LP) problems: the ability to find low-accuracy solutions quickly. While such solutions may not be applicable in all applications of LP, one possible use is to accelerate heuristics for finding feasible solutions to Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) problems, where these approximate LP solutions can hopefully guide a heuristic towards accurate and high-quality MIP solutions. While a monolithic heuristic that exploits PDHG solutions would be useful, we pose a broader question here: could we replace the default LP solver in a modern MIP solver with PDHG to accelerate most (or all) of its existing heuristics? We find that doing so does have some obvious drawbacks, preventing us from using several powerful MIP techniques, but it leaves most others unaffected, ultimately resulting in a heuristic that often finds high-quality, high-accuracy solutions faster than current state-of-the-art strategies.
paper.title: Using a MIP Solver as a PDHG-Based MIP Heuristic

paper.abstract: Natural language interfaces can greatly benefit the accessibility and usability of optimization modeling, and recent advances in large language models (LLMs) show promise in automatically translating textual problem descriptions into executable solver formulations. However, a key challenge for existing approaches is to ensure that the inferred formulation correctly implements the intended task, even if it may execute without errors. We introduce VeriSimpl, a solver LLM framework for robust natural-language-to-optimization formalization. Our approach is based on the idea of simplification-based verification, where the optimization solver is leveraged to generate simplified diagnostic queries about a candidate formulation to allow the LLM to tractably reason about the correctness of the formulation with respect to the task description. We present such simplification strategies along different dimensions with respect to problem constraints and decision variables, which allow the LLM to reason locally under fixed global contexts. Evaluations on a range of optimization benchmarks show how our approach provides consistent improvements in accuracy over existing methods, while also providing a novel high-precision self-verification signal.
paper.comment: Accepted and published at ICML 2026. Code available at https://github.com/suabar/VeriSimple
paper.title: VeriSimpl: Robust Optimization Modeling from Natural Language using Simplification-based Verification

analysis.analysis: 作者将问题建模为智能体与环境（模型、训练实例、验证工具）的迭代交互：智能体分析原模型并应用潜在优化策略，每次提出候选模型后由自动化验证程序检查其解注入原模型后的可行性，并在训练实例上比较求解器性能；若验证失败则诊断并修复。方法不依赖预定义的规则库或问题结构分解，而是依赖大语言模型的推理能力与经验评估信号。

analysis.relation_to_research: 该论文属于人工智能驱动运筹优化（AI4OR）中自动建模的方向，与生产调度中的约束模型构建和重构有具体迁移路径：调度问题常以 CP 模型表达，而模型选择（如对称性破除、全局约束、变量表示）对求解时间影响显著。论文的智能体框架可直接用于自动改进调度问题的 CP 模型，但迁移需要条件：需将生产调度问题编码为 CPMpy 模型并提供少量小规模训练实例，且需验证生成的模型在大规模调度实例上的泛化与求解质量。需要指出，论文实验未涉及生产调度或柔性作业车间等具体场景，以上迁移为推测。论文的验证-修复机制与经验正确性保证思路，也可为学习辅助搜索中的模型正确性校验提供参考。
analysis.setting: 研究问题为自动改进约束规划（CP）模型：用户以 CPMpy 建模库提供原始约束模型以及三个小规模训练实例，目标是在固定求解时限内自动获得一个修改后的模型，使其在保持与原模型解集可行（即解注入原模型后仍可行）的前提下提升优化目标质量。决策对象是模型的结构性变换（如对称性破除、隐含约束、全局约束、变量表示与约束重构）。关键约束包括：只考虑优化问题（以固定时间限制内的目标质量衡量性能）、训练实例仅三个且较小、正确性必须经验验证而非构造性证明、智能体运行最多 80 步且无固定时间限制。信息假设为智能体可访问原始模型、三个训练实例以及验证工具，测试实例仅在评估阶段使用。环境为静态的离线模型改进问题，但引入迭代诊断-修复的动态智能体流程。

analysis.why_recommended: 虽然论文不直接研究生产调度问题，但它提出了一种将大语言模型智能体用于约束模型自动重构与改进的框架，并强调经验正确性验证与迭代诊断-修复。这与当前研究中自动建模、学习辅助搜索以及大模型智能体优化方向高度相关，其验证-修复循环、正确性经验验证、基于少量训练实例的泛化评估等机制，可为生产调度问题的自动建模与模型改进提供可借鉴的方法论。同时，论文诚实地报告非智能体基线达到相近改进率，对评估智能体方法的实际贡献具有警示价值，有助于研究者在公平计算预算下审视智能体机制的必要性。

paper.abstract: The runtime of Constraint Programming (CP) solvers is highly sensitive to modeling choices, such as symmetry breaking, implied constraints, global constraints, constraint reformulation, and variable representation. Improving these constraint models has traditionally required human expertise, and existing automated reformulation systems are restricted to a predefined library of hand-crafted transformation rules. We introduce an agentic framework that instead reformulates a constraint model from an open-ended space and establishes correctness empirically rather than by construction: a Large Language Model (LLM) agent, given a model and three training instances, proposes alternative formulations, validates each by injecting its solution back into the original model, and diagnoses and repairs failures, returning the best variant it finds in a median of about fifteen minutes. The models are expressed in the CPMpy modeling library, and each proposed model is evaluated on three larger test instances. Across nine combinatorial optimization problems, the generated models outperform the originals on 21 of 27 test instances, and on some problems solve more than two orders of magnitude faster. A comparison against non-agentic baselines that reuse the same validation and selection tools indicates that the gains stem from the agent's iterative diagnosis and repair, not merely from sampling several candidates. These results demonstrate that autonomous agentic methods can support the improvement of constraint models.
paper.title: Improving Constraint Models with LLM Agents

analysis.analysis: 作者将问题结构化为多模型族生成、跨实例最优值一致性分组以及基于求解器验证问题拟合阈值的准入决策。具体而言，从三个模型族生成模型，在原始问题与重采样参数实例上运行，保留在所有实例上跨族最优值一致的最大模型组，并用求解器验证问题拟合的阈值来决定接受、弃权或上报，同时给出接受值中假发现率的有限样本上界。对假发现案例的审计进一步定位到基准文本对复现标签答案所需数字的省略或舍入，并设计了对提取数字与文本进行对照的无标签检查。
challenges: 在无真实最优标签的问题流上无法直接判定生成的优化模型是否正确

执行成功或单实例一致性等无标签代理会接受错误模型
在基准文本省略或舍入关键数字时，无标签证书会产生假发现
有限样本的假发现率界在标定集成立但在基准流上不一定成立

analysis.insight: 核心洞察在于：一个候选模型的正确性信号如果来自学习器外部、并且在不同模型族之间对同一问题及重采样实例的最优值达成一致，那么它比学习器自身的多数投票或单纯执行成功更可靠。作者通过消融说明增益来自“被接受的值外在于学习器且跨模型族一致”，而重采样在该数据流上从未改变已接受值、只降低覆盖率，说明一致性校验与外部化才是关键，而非简单增加实例数量。

analysis.motivation: 从经验中学习的智能体通过存储已求解轨迹并作为技能复用，可以提升优化建模能力；但错误轨迹一旦进入技能库会被反复检索，而在新问题流上没有真实答案可用于判断对错。现有学习器依靠已知最优值或标签进行准入，无标签替代方案如执行成功或单实例一致性可能接受错误模型，因此需要一种无标签的准入机制。
analysis.primary_topic: 大语言模型智能体优化建模中的无标签轨迹准入与经验学习
analysis.relation_to_research: 该论文直接面向 AI4OR 中的优化建模环节，属于大语言模型智能体自动建模与经验学习方向，与自动建模、学习辅助求解、智能体优化密切相关。其无标签准入与多模型族一致性思路可迁移到生产调度中的模型/策略库管理，例如在柔性作业车间或流水车间中需要判断由 LLM 或学习器生成的调度模型、约束或启发式规则是否可信时，可借鉴其准入-弃权-上报机制；但迁移到动态扰动、能效与多目标约束的生产调度场景仍为推测，需要额外条件：需要可运行并比较的求解器或仿真器，需要定义跨模型族一致性的目标值，并需要针对调度问题重新拟合阈值与验证假发现率界。论文未在调度或组合优化求解上做实验，因此其结论对生产调度的直接有效性尚无证据。
analysis.setting: 研究问题是在只有问题陈述、没有真实最优答案标签的流式场景下，判断大语言模型智能体生成的优化建模轨迹是否可以进入经验/技能库以供后续复用。决策对象是每条候选轨迹的准入、弃权或上报。目标是提升准入精度并控制错误模型被接受的风险，进而提高下游建模准确率。关键约束是缺乏 ground-truth 最优值，且基准文本可能省略或舍入复现答案所需的数字。信息假设是可在求解器上运行生成的模型，并可在重采样参数的实例上比较不同模型族给出的最优值。环境被明确描述为不断到来的新问题流（stream），属于动态在线场景。
analysis.title_zh: 无答案准入：面向大语言模型优化建模的无标签认证与经验学习
analysis.uncertainty: 证据范围仅为标题与摘要，未提供全文，因此无法确认网络结构、提示设计、三个模型族的具体身份、阈值拟合细节、基准名称与实例规模、计算预算是否公平、统计显著性以及跨问题族的泛化表现；相关性判断基于其明确的 AI4OR 优化建模主题，但未验证其方法在调度类问题上的效果。
analysis.why_recommended: 对研究智能优化与 AI4OR 的博士生而言，该文提供了一个可迁移的机制：在无真实标签的动态问题流中，如何用外部模型族一致性与阈值化准入来控制经验库污染。其关于假发现率界、覆盖率与准入精度权衡的分析，以及公平比较不同无标签替代方案的做法，对学习辅助搜索、自动建模和智能体优化中的可靠性与复现性研究具有参考价值。

paper.abstract: Agents that learn from experience improve at optimization modeling by storing solved trajectories and reusing them as skills. A wrong trajectory that enters the library can be retrieved again and again, and on a stream of new problems there is no ground-truth answer to decide with. Existing learners admit trajectories by matching known optima or labels, and label-free substitutes such as execution success or agreement at one instance can admit wrong models. We introduce ADMITOR, a label-free admission gate. It generates models from three model families, runs each on the stated problem and on instances with resampled parameters, keeps the largest group of models whose optimal values agree on every instance across families, and applies a threshold fitted on solver-verified problems to accept, abstain, or escalate, with a finite-sample bound on the false-discovery rate among accepted values. Inside a state-of-the-art skill learner, ADMITOR raises candidate-level admission precision to 0.927, against 0.871 for majority vote over the host's own samples and 0.726 for execution success, and its library, the smallest of the four, reaches the highest macro accuracy over five public benchmarks, 58.4 against 54.8 for majority vote. An ablation on the same records shows that the gain comes from the accepted value being external to the learner and unanimous across families; on this stream, resampling never changed an accepted value and only reduced coverage. The false-discovery bound holds on the calibration set but not on the benchmark stream: an audit of every false certificate traces most of them to benchmark texts that omit or round the numbers needed to reproduce the labeled answer, and a label-free check of the extracted numbers against the text flags most of these cases.
paper.comment: Code and data are available at https://github.com/junbolian/AdmitOR
paper.title: Admission Without Answers: Label-Free Certification and Experience Learning for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling

paper.abstract: Combinatorial scheduling poses a significant challenge for language models, requiring them to identify feasible solutions within exponentially large search spaces while satisfying complex constraints. This challenge is especially pronounced in resource-constrained settings, where larger language models are impractical and selection is limited to smaller models which often fail to preserve feasibility when scheduling directly from natural language. To address these limitations, we introduce SDDL, a neuro-symbolic framework that translates natural-language scheduling problems into compact, solver-aligned representations of tasks, resources, constraints, and objectives, while delegating low-level modeling and search to a deterministic compiler and external solver. On a 300-instance, multi-family subset of scheduling problems, SDDL improves independently verified feasibility for every resource-constrained model tested. The two strongest SDDL configurations reach 55.3% and 28.3%, up from direct-generation baselines of 23.7% and 1.3% and solver-code baselines of 21.7% and 7.0%, with a 0.0% median optimality gap among feasible schedules. By expressing problem structure rather than generating solutions or solver code, SDDL enables smaller models to approach the strongest evaluated direct- and solver-code configurations, including substantially larger frontier models.
paper.comment: To appear, The 4th Annual Workshop on Mathematical Natural Language Processing (MathNLP2026) @EMNLP2026
paper.title: Improving Natural-Language Combinatorial-Optimization Accuracy in Resource-Constrained Language Models via Formal Abstractions

paper.abstract: Developments in high-performance computing (HPC) technology continue to drastically increase quantities of available processing power. In the context of digital evolution, this explosive growth offers opportunities to advance both hypothesis-driven explorations of multi-scale biological phenomena and application-driven evolutionary optimization targeting hard problem domains. A particular opportunity arises from emerging next-generation AI/ML hardware accelerator platforms, such as the 880,000-processor Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE). Such hardware, however, constrains on-device data storage and movement --- a challenge compounded by vulnerability to failures arising over numerous device components. Best-effort relaxations that depart from a traditional deterministic computing paradigm can help accommodate such constraints, but complicate reproducibility and risk introducing artifactual biases. We explore these concerns, developing a framework to measure runtime behavior of best-effort code and examining case studies of best-effort computing in digital evolution projects. The first case study applies best-effort CPU-cluster multiprocessing to a multicellularity evolution model, which provides 92% scaling efficiency at 64 processes ($2.1\times$ speedup) and exhibits robust median quality of service, even under hardware anomalies. The second case study examines WSE-based simulations, demonstrating best-effort strategies to track spatiotemporal population history --- through sparse, asynchronous device-to-host sampling that tolerates hardware faults. In sum, across potential forms and scopes of best-effort relaxation, we argue that digital evolution is uniquely positioned to contribute in developing post-deterministic HPC paradigms.
paper.title: Trust, but Verify: Rigorously Profiling Best-Effort High-Performance Computing for Digital Evolution

analysis.analysis: 作者通过区分两个使用层级来分离记忆与泛化能力：第 1 级给模型单个问题实例并要求返回该实例的解，第 2 级只给问题类描述与参数范围并要求返回从实例参数到解的算法，且算法在评估前固定。通过这种分层评估，作者得以判断性能提升究竟来自对具体实例的拟合，还是来自对问题类的可泛化算法设计能力。同时作者以最强模型 gpt-5.6-sol 与现有最佳方法在多个运筹问题上对比，并观察不同发布时间模型之间的性能变化。问题结构、下界或图表示等具体分析手段材料未说明。

仅有未调优的单一提示且计算预算固定，限制了人工引导和试错空间
需要公平比较模型生成算法与专用方法的计算预算与求解质量

paper.abstract: We ask whether large language models (LLMs) can design effective algorithms for well-specified operations research (OR) problems. We study inventory control, queueing network control, and assortment optimization. We evaluate two levels of LLM use: at level 1, the model receives one problem instance and returns a solution for that instance; at level 2, it receives only the problem class description and broad parameter ranges, and returns an algorithm that maps instance parameters to solutions. Human input is minimal: we give one untuned prompt that describes the problem, and the model has access to a Python sandbox tool with a fixed compute budget. The strongest model we test, gpt-5.6-sol, matches or outperforms the best existing method on almost all evaluated instances. This holds even at level 2, where the returned algorithm is fixed before seeing the evaluation instances. Performance also improves sharply across models released less than eight months apart, suggesting that this capability is moving quickly. Thus, for the well-specified operations problems we study, a single untuned LLM query can already produce algorithms competitive with specialized methods. These results suggest that frontier LLMs can be a serious empirical baseline for algorithm design in well-specified OR problems.
paper.title: LLMs Can Design Near-Optimal OR Algorithms

paper.abstract: Quantum hardware is beginning to address structured combinatorial optimisation, but two steps still block practical use: mapping real operational models onto hardware-compatible instances, and converting noisy hardware output back into feasible decisions. Here we introduce a backend-agnostic computational interface that compiles the discrete decision layer of stochastic unit commitment into a move-based maximum-weight independent set (MWIS) problem, while retaining continuous dispatch and feasibility recovery in the classical computational layer. We validate the approach in a green hydrogen scheduling setting and deploy it on the QuEra Aquila neutral-atom quantum processor. This is the first end-to-end industrial scheduling workflow that connects real operational decisions to programmable neutral-atom hardware through a solver-agnostic MWIS representation. Across a 15-day hardware campaign on 50-node instances, hardware-generated solutions after classical refinement match or exceed the dispatch margins obtained from exact MWIS on every day. When scaling to 144 nodes, encoding quality remains stable, while the probability that the full atom array survives, rather than graph embedding, emerges as the dominant bottleneck to further scaling. Together, these results establish a hardware-compatible computational pathway toward larger problem scales, and lay the groundwork for exploring regimes in which exact classical optimisation may no longer scale efficiently.
paper.title: A Backend-Agnostic MWIS Kernel for Stochastic Unit Commitment with Neutral-Atom Hardware Validation

analysis.analysis: 作者通过理论分析揭示离线优化的本质需求：不需要整个函数的学习，而只需在优化轨迹上准确。他们提出了算法依赖的可学习性概念，并证明了在若干代表性离散和连续设定下，该可学习性是充分的。基于此动机，他们形式化了轨迹学习框架，将问题分解为轨迹构建、轨迹建模和候选生成，并指出现有方法在该框架下的位置。进一步提出UGTL，利用条件扩散模型对局部连贯的改进轨迹建模，并通过多样性候选集生成提高性能。

paper.abstract: Black-Box Optimization (BBO) has broad applications, while traditional algorithms such as evolutionary algorithms and Bayesian optimization face efficiency challenges as real-world BBO problems grow increasingly complex. Data-driven optimization has been the most popular paradigm to improve the efficiency of BBO, by learning from data. Offline data-driven optimization seeks high-quality solutions using only a fixed set of previous evaluations, attracting substantial attention because it requires no additional online evaluations. Many offline optimization methods have been proposed, but a fundamental question remains unanswered: what learnability is sufficient for offline optimization? Prior theoretical studies show that Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learnability is insufficient, as the optimal region may remain poorly learned even when most regions are well learned. In this paper, we propose algorithm-dependent learnability, which requires accuracy only on the optimizer's trajectory. We prove that its value-query form is sufficient for representative discrete settings, including greedy and local search for submodular maximization, while its first-order analogue is sufficient for projected gradient descent on convex minimization. Motivated by this notion, we formalize a trajectory-learning framework comprising trajectory construction, trajectory modeling, and candidate generation, and analyze existing trajectory-based methods under it. We further propose Uncertainty-aware Gradient-guided Trajectory Learning (UGTL), which constructs locally coherent improvement trajectories reflecting plausible search paths, models them with conditional diffusion, and selects a diverse candidate set. Our experiments show that UGTL achieves the best average rank, 3.1/25, among 25 methods on Design-Bench tasks, and confirm that our trajectory construction plays a significant role in the improvement.
paper.title: Rethinking Learnability in Offline Data-driven Optimization

analysis.analysis: 材料未详细说明作者如何从理论上分析问题，但摘要表明作者将生成式排序重新表述为物品与位置之间的二部匹配问题，利用匈牙利算法求解最优分配。这种表述利用了排列的约束结构，将解码从生成问题转化为优化问题。作者进一步通过系统研究训练信号和骨干适配，分解了架构、训练信号和骨干适配的贡献，以理解各因素对质量和速度的影响。

analysis.insight: 核心洞察在于生成式排序的输出空间是排列结构，而非任意文本；因此不必从左到右逐个生成序数，而是可以从LLM的预填充隐藏状态中一次性提取所有物品的位置分数，将解码转化为一个组合优化问题（最优二部匹配）。通过匈牙利算法直接得到有效排列，避免了自回归的串行依赖，也不需要修复步骤，从而将前向传播次数从O(N)降至O(1)。

method: SPD解码策略：设计为单遍前向传播（O(1)），读取LLM预填充隐藏状态上的N×K物品-位置分数矩阵。
使用轻量级自注意力头从隐藏状态中提取分数矩阵。
将序数解码为矩阵的最优二部分配，采用匈牙利算法保证生成有效排列。
训练方法：采用LoRA微调LLM骨干，并结合自回归LLM排序蒸馏，以对齐教师模型的排序质量。
架构：结合轻量级解码头和骨干适配（如LoRA）实现端到端推理。
analysis.motivation: 大型语言模型在生成式排序中达到最先进质量，但其自回归解码每个输出词元需要一次顺序前向传播，导致推理延迟高。作者观察到排序器只需输出N个序数值，且其排列结构允许更高效的解码，因此希望利用这种格式特性打破自回归的顺序瓶颈，实现实时排序。
analysis.primary_topic: 利用组合优化加速大型语言模型的生成式排序解码
analysis.relation_to_research: 论文事实：本文属于AI4OR方向，将生成式排序与组合优化联系，利用匈牙利算法进行O(1)解码，属于学习辅助搜索或优化结合LLM的实例。推测：该方法可能迁移到生产调度中的排列问题，例如工件排序或作业排序，其中需要输出排列且可建模为二部匹配；但迁移条件是需要有预训练LLM或类似序列模型产生分数矩阵，且问题结构需能映射为物品-位置二部图。此外，其高效的解码机制对未来实时调度中的LLM辅助决策具有启发意义。
analysis.setting: 研究问题是如何高效解码大语言模型生成的排序结果。决策对象是待排序的N个物品的序数序列。目标是设计一种解码策略，使得生成排序仅需O(1)次前向传播，同时保持与自回归教师模型相当的排序质量。关键约束是解码必须产生有效的排列（即无重复且完整的序数序列），不允许通过修复产生。信息假设是LLM的预填充隐藏状态包含足够的排序信息。环境是静态的，因为排序针对固定的一组物品。
analysis.title_zh: SPD：用于生成式重排序的单遍解码
analysis.uncertainty: 摘要未提供作者单位、通讯作者信息，也未提供实验细节如基线、数据集、排序质量指标、消融的具体数值，因此无法全面评估其实验严格性和泛化能力。此外，没有全文节选，无法验证方法的具体实现细节和潜在局限性。
analysis.why_recommended: 本文展示了如何针对特定输出结构设计专用解码策略，将生成模型的采样转化为组合优化求解，实现数量级的速度提升。对于研究学习辅助搜索的学者，该方法提供了一种将神经网络输出与匈牙利算法结合的新范式；对于生产调度，虽然问题不同，但其思想可启发将约束优化嵌入解码过程，值得关注其机制设计。

paper.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve state-of-the-art generative ranking quality, but the ranking they produce must be decoded, and autoregressive decoding spends one sequential forward pass per emitted token. We observe that the only tokens a ranker must emit are the $N$ ordinal values naming the items in ranked order, and that this narrow, permutation-structured output format admits decoding strategies which are much more efficient than left-to-right generation. We introduce SPD (Single Forward Pass), a format-specialized decoding strategy that decodes all $N$ ordinals in $O(1)$ forward passes. SPD reads an $N \times K$ item-position score matrix off the LLM's prefill hidden states with a lightweight self-attention head, then decodes the ordinals as the optimal bipartite assignment of that matrix via the Hungarian algorithm, yielding a valid permutation by construction rather than by repair. Through a systematic study of training signals and backbone adaptation, we show that LoRA-based fine-tuning combined with auto-regressive LLM ranking distillation reaches 28 ms end-to-end inference, a speed-up of 64x while maintaining ranking quality on par with the teacher. We provide a complete ablation decomposing the contributions of architecture, training signal, and backbone adaptation. Our framework connects generative ranking to combinatorial optimization, opening a path toward other $O(1)$-decode mechanisms for real-time ranking.
paper.title: SPD: Single Pass Decoding for Generative Reranking

analysis.analysis: 作者将问题形式化为带随机需求的联合补货问题，采用深度RL框架，利用可微分的库存模拟器计算路径梯度，直接对订货量进行梯度传播。架构上采用物品排列等变Transformer，以捕捉物品间的依赖关系，并保持等变性以提高泛化和扩展性。该设计使梯度能跨时间步和动作维度有效传播，避免了传统策略梯度方法在高维动作空间中的高方差问题。
challenges: 高维观测和动作空间（超过1e4和1e3维度）导致滚动时域MILP求解缓慢
标准RL在高维动作空间中的信用分配困难
共享固定成本在零和正订货量之间产生不连续性，挑战连续动作RL方法

evidence.claim: 在线决策时间相对MILP大幅缩短
evidence.quote: It also reduces online decision-making time by over 4 million times relative to MILP solvers, enabling real-time, large-scale deep RL in supply chain operations.

evidence.claim: 作者提出物品排列等变Transformer和通过库存动态的路径梯度训练
evidence.quote: with an item-permutation-equivariant Transformer architecture and pathwise-gradient training through the inventory dynamics

experiments: 对比基线包括多种学习算法（如MLP、Transformer-PPO）和滚动时域MILP（Gurobi）
